summary: Second section 4 test-only repair of documented step M4-S05, on top of the first (F-59, envelope 2026-09-12T17-06-24Z.json, deploy-order.md section 8), for F-60 (reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md run 5): wrapping the fixture inserts themselves in System.runAs(agent) failed FLS on Subject, Origin, AccountId, Priority and EntitlementId, none of which Case_Agent_Core/Case_Tier1 grant Edit on -- only Severity__c. Per skills/apex/test-class-standards/references/gotchas.md Gotcha 15, every fixture insert in CaseMilestoneServiceTest (Account, Entitlement, every Case row) now runs through TestDataFactory.insertAsSystem(...) outside System.runAs(agent); only the action under test (the Status change that fires CaseMilestoneTrigger, and the CaseMilestoneService.completeMilestones calls that stand in for it in the other three methods) still runs inside System.runAs(agent). TestDataFactory.cls was refreshed to a verbatim copy of the current template (commit be09a7bff, which added insertAsSystem since the section 8 copy at commit 5edcb3281). No assertion, message string, or Test.startTest/stopTest boundary was added, removed or changed. CaseMilestoneService.cls, CaseMilestoneTrigger.trigger and TestUserFactory.cls are unchanged byte for byte since section 8.
confidence_rationale: Both declared and requested checkers exit 0 (check_entitlement_apex_hooks.py --strict: 5 files, 0 ERROR/0 WARN; check_test_class_standards.py --strict: score 100, 0 findings). check-outputs is ok on all 8 declared paths, and both copied template classes diff empty against their canonical sources. Confidence stays at MEDIUM, not HIGH, because: (1) no offline Apex compiler exists (agents/apex-builder/GATES.md Gate D) and this build has no target_org_alias, so this repair is confirmed only by the operator's next dry run (run 6), not executed by this agent; (2) whether the persona's own FLS is sufficient for the action under test (the trigger's write to CaseMilestone.CompletionDate) remains unverified without an org, unaffected by this repair either way; and (3) this is the second repair to the same defect class (F-59 then F-60) in one session, which is itself evidence the first repair's diagnosis was incomplete rather than proof this one is exhaustive.

process_observations.observation: Both the declared checker and the requested check_test_class_standards.py run clean under --strict on the first attempt this time, and check-outputs confirms all 8 declared paths are still present -- the repair is auditable as a small, targeted diff rather than a rewrite.

This is the second time in one session that a repair aimed at running the test as the permissioned persona (section 8, F-59) itself needed a second repair (section 9, F-60) because the first pass conflated fields the persona's own code path writes with fields a fixture needs populated to be meaningful. Gotcha 15 was authored from this exact finding, per its own 'Where this came from' note, which suggests the distinction is genuinely non-obvious rather than a one-off oversight in this step.

Five milestone verifications, every checker, and two org dry runs passed the section 8 repair before run 5 caught F-60, because nothing in the library asserted that an object grant (Case Create) is accompanied by field grants on the standard fields a persona's layouts and processes actually populate. That gap is named in run 5's own finding as a library gap, not only a this-build gap.

Whether Case_Agent_Core plus Case_Tier1 grant sufficient FLS for the action under test -- the trigger's indirect write to CaseMilestone.CompletionDate -- is unverified in a design-only build and is unaffected by this repair either way, since system mode only changes how the fixture is seeded, not what the persona can do afterward.
